LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
 <security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practice for a prebuilt (`-bin`) package. All binary downloads come from the official upstream project (github.com/feenkcom/gtoolkit) over HTTPS, and the x86_64 and aarch64 archives have pinned sha256 checksums, so those downloads are integrity-verified. The `package()` function only creates standard install directories, extracts the upstream zip into `$pkgdir/opt/glamorous-toolkit` with bsdtar, installs a maintainer-written launcher script and .desktop file, and creates a symlink for the CLI binary. No `eval`, no base64/obfuscated commands, no build-time network requests, no writes outside `$srcdir`/`$pkgdir`, and no credential or data access exist anywhere in the file.

Hygiene notes (non-malicious): the launcher script's checksum is `SKIP`, so its contents are not integrity-verified at build time, and the launcher itself is a separate source item not visible in this file. This is a reproducibility/hygiene concern, not evidence of malice — the launcher is a local file distributed with the AUR package, and a SKIP checksum alone must not trigger an UNSAFE verdict. No other red flags are present.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard bin packaging; official upstream with pinned checksums; no malicious behavior found.</summary>
</security_assessment>
